birth.note: doxologia.ro: «Părintele Sofronie (Serghei Simeonovici) Saharov s-a născut pe 23 septembrie 1896, în familia unor credincioși ortodocși din Moscova, Rusia.»

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Părintele Sofronie Saharov a trecut la cele veșnice în ziua de 11 iulie 1993, la vârsta de aproape 97 de ani.»

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 11 iulie — «Sfântul Cuvios Sofronie de la Essex»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Σωφρόνιος του Έσσεξ»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the dates and the name in the world agree with it exactly: «Οσιος Σωφρονιος Του Εσσεξ (1896 - 1993)», Sergei Semyonovich Sakharov, born at Moscow 22 September 1896 and reposed 11 July 1993. He is none of the corpus's many men named Sophronius. The Greek page differs from the Romanian in one detail of the date of birth — it prints 22 September where doxologia printed 23 September — and the folder's `dates` carry only the year, which both agree on, so no change to `dates` is proposed and the disagreement is recorded here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence; the page prints verses to him but no apolytikion, so no hymn is taken.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Fiu preadorit te-ai arătat, Preafericite, lui Siluan, Preacuviosului Părinte, dascăl fiind, Sofronie, de cele cerești, în Apus ai strălucit cu a ta înțelepciune și, prin sfântă viața ta, la lumină mânat-ai pe cei ce Tată Îl numesc pe Dumnezeu, pe Care cândva vedea-L-vom, prin ruga Ta.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Sofronie de la Essex», Glasul 4

english.text: A most beloved son you were shown to be, most blessed one, to Silouan the venerable father; and being yourself a teacher of heavenly things, Sophrony, you shone in the West by your wisdom, and by your holy life you led into the light those who call God their Father — whom one day we shall see, through your prayer.
